symptom: The world WebSocket sent one snapshot and then nothing. wrangler tail showed one alarm (wall 1285 ms, cpu 505 ms) and then a canceled alarm. setAlarm was the last statement of alarm(), so a throw, cancel, or overrun ended the loop.
root_causes_seen_in_tail: Dynamic worker concurrency limit exceeded: each request may have up to 10 concurrent dynamic worker invocations. All creatures were stepped with one Promise.all.
Some creature steps ran longer than the tick.

fix.alarm_first: src/worker/world.ts alarm() calls setAlarm before tick() and catches tick errors
fix.bounded_work: src/worker/tick.ts: at most 8 creatures stepped per tick, round-robin over the rest; 500 ms per step via withTimeout; 50 ms CPU limit per Dynamic Worker
fix.isolation: runSteps logs and penalizes a failing or slow creature and continues
fix.rearm_on_connect: World.fetch calls ensureAlarm before anything else; nextAlarmAt re-arms a stale or far-future alarm
fix.loop: Alarm alone fired every 1.4 to 10 s under load, and once the isolate hit its memory limit and reset. The tick now runs on an in-memory setTimeout loop (nextTickDelay subtracts the tick's own time). The alarm is a 5 s watchdog that restarts the loop after an eviction or reset, and every WebSocket connect calls ensureAlarm and startLoop.
fix.broadcast_first: the snapshot is broadcast at the start of each tick, before creature steps

proof.tool: headless Chrome via puppeteer-core, CDP Network.webSocketFrameReceived
proof.gate: latest runs: 20 snapshot frames in 30 s, 18 with position change: passed
proof.note: First run right after deploy had 13 frames while the object restarted from the code update; the next runs had 15, 20, and 20.

tuning: With 19 creatures, 16 per tick in two chunks of 8 overran the tick (8 frames in 30 s), so the cap became one chunk of 8.
